chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:

about a man who touches something from the woman, would that spoil his fast or break it? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is disliked for the young man for fear that the semen may precede (discharge).'
ai.seo_question: Does touching one's wife break the fast during Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on foreplay during Ramadan, distinguishing between mere touching and acts leading to seminal discharge. He advises that it is disliked (*makruh*) for a young man prone to premature ejaculation to engage in such intimacy, as the resulting discharge breaks the fast, whereas for those who can control themselves, it may not necessarily invalidate it. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that breaking the fast requires actual emission, not just the act of foreplay itself, highlighting the importance of self-awareness in religious observance.
